newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes surge higher, May widens lead on June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes surge higher, May widens lead on June.

text.p: Cash crudes continued to display strength across the board in U.S. trading Friday, benefitting from refiner position-squaring.

Specifically, sweet crudes have gained on the firming prices demanded for North Sea barrels. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James shrunk the discount it holds to the outright benchmark to only 10-15 cents, traders said.

"There are no North Sea sweet cargoes for arrival in ealy May, except for maybe an Oseberg. Generally, the May program has been absorbed, forcing refiners to come in and cover up," said a cash dealer in Houston.
May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around 40-45 cents higher at $19.80-90 a barrel. May/June spreads have increased sharply, now favoring a surging May by 20-22 cts.
May/June spreads went off the board Thursday at only a 10 cts premium to the front month, ending weeks of contango status for the market
Usual market conditions favor the front month over later months, putting prices in backwardation, the state May again finds itself to the June.
Traders said May strength is relative, noting how weak the front month has been. "It may seem dramatic today, but it doesn't seem like anything more than book squaring," a trader said.
For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James stood around a 15 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing, selling between a 10-20 cts discount from the start of business today.
Sources said spread trades for Eugene Island-LLS/St. James also moved the sweet grade to firmer differentials, possibly signalling a general trend for dumping sours in favor of sweet, traders said.
Other price levels saw West Texas Sour/Midland around $1.75-$1.85 under the benchmark and Midland/WTI valued at 30 cts below level.
